flashcard_questions.q: What is the chain of command in a business?
flashcard_questions.a: The line of authority running from the top of the business to the bottom.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the span of control?
flashcard_questions.a: The number of subordinates a manager is directly responsible for.

flashcard_questions.q: What is delegation in a business?
flashcard_questions.a: Giving a task to a lower-level employee.
Removing one or more layers of management to cut costs and speed up communication.
A structure with many layers of management and a long chain of command.
A structure with few layers of management and wide spans of control.
A document setting out the duties and responsibilities of a role.
A document listing the qualifications and personal qualities a candidate needs.

flashcard_questions.q: What did Frederick Taylor believe motivates workers?
What is the top level of Maslow's hierarchy of needs?
Which level of Maslow's hierarchy does a wage satisfy?
What did Herzberg call the factors that only prevent dissatisfaction?
What is the communication advantage of a flat structure?
flashcard_questions.a: Messages travel faster because there are fewer levels to pass through.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the main communication drawback of a hierarchical structure?
flashcard_questions.a: It is slow, because messages must pass through many layers.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is internal recruitment cheaper than external recruitment?
flashcard_questions.a: There are no advertising costs and no induction is needed.

notes: 15 cards: 8 term→definition (chain of command, span of control, delegation, delayering, hierarchical, flat, job description, person specification), 4 theorist→claim cards (Taylor, Maslow top level, Maslow physiological, Herzberg hygiene factors), 3 single-fact advantage/disadvantage cards. The seven recruitment stages and the five Maslow levels were not made into list cards — enumeration answers break Rule 2.
